evidence.quote: A personal access token allows access to the api for the user who created it.
Returns the user records for all users in all workspaces and organizations accessible to the authenticated user.
When more results exist, the response includes a `next_page` with an `offset`
Retrieve the audit log events that have been captured in your domain.

assumptions: The workspace ID is asked from the customer as a connection setting, because the source does not show a call that lists workspaces.
The user list in the source only shows id and name. Requesting email through opt_fields is assumed to work but is not shown in the source.
The source shows no status, role, or last-active field on users, so those are left empty. It is unconfirmed whether deactivated users are returned.
The audit log is the usage signal. The source does not state which plan it needs. 'Enterprise' is an assumption and should be checked.
Audit log events are matched to people by the actor's email address. Events by non-user actors (Asana, anonymous) will have no matching person.
The maximum page size is not documented. 100 is used for users, and the documented default of 1000 for audit log events.
The source states no rate limits, so none are configured.
The audit log is assumed to need a service account or admin token; the source does not list the exact scopes.
